---
title: "Data quality"
---

*Status: v0.1 (milestone M2 in progress). This is the project's running
register of known problems with the
[data sources](data-sources.qmd). It is expected to grow as sources are
ingested in earnest.*

## What this report covers

The [roadmap](../ROADMAP.md) asks for a register of **known gaps,
revisions, suppressions, and definitional breaks**. Anything that would
mislead a reader who trusted a number at face value belongs here.

## Known gaps

- **Determinants and stratifiers.** Income, education, and employment are
  used to stratify results (see the
  [measurement framework](measurement-framework.qmd)); BC Stats, the BC
  Data Catalogue, Statistics Canada, and K-12 reporting are catalogued as
  their sources. They are **determinants, not health outcomes**, and are
  never reported as health on their own.
- **Microdata access.** Individual-level sources are catalogued as
  [access routes](data-sources.qmd#microdata-access-routes) (Population
  Data BC; Statistics Canada Research Data Centres) but no approvals are
  in place yet, so the catalogue is aggregate-only in practice. Nothing
  individual-level may enter the repository regardless.
- **Neighbourhood-level health indicators.** Population denominators exist
  at LHA/neighbourhood resolution, but health outcomes are not yet
  catalogued below health-authority level.
- **External drivers.** Cross-border patient flows and supply-chain
  pressures are identified as relevant but have **no catalogued source**
  yet; the wildfire, demographic, and macro series are the current
  stand-ins.
- **Social wellbeing.** Measures of social connection and belonging are
  sparse and carried on a small number of survey series only.

## Revisions and provisional figures

- **Substance-use mortality** is published provisionally and revised
  upward as investigations conclude [@bccdcDrugs]. Preliminary and final
  figures must never be pooled without noting the vintage.
- **Cancer statistics** for the most recent years are typically incomplete
  because of registration lag [@bcCancer].
- **Population estimates** at sub-provincial levels are revised as
  administrative sources update; rates computed on them inherit the
  revision.
- **National survey estimates** carry sampling error and are occasionally
  revised after release [@statcan].

## Suppression

- **Small-area counts** (e.g. vital statistics by small geography) are
  suppressed for privacy [@bcStatsVital]. Suppressed cells are missing,
  not zero; treating them as zero biases rates.

## Definitional breaks (regime shifts)

These are candidates for the **regime-aware reporting** required by
milestone M3; each marks a point where a series before and after is
effectively different.

| Break | Affected sources | Implication |
|-------|------------------|-------------|
| Cause-of-death coding revisions (ICD revisions) | Vital Statistics; national mortality | Cause-specific mortality series are not directly comparable across the revision boundary |
| Declared public-health emergency (2016) | BCCDC substance-use dashboard; overdose response | Surveillance expanded at the emergency; counts before and after reflect different detection intensity |
| COVID-19 pandemic (2020–) | mortality, morbidity, mental health | Both a real shock and a measurement shock (care disruption, coding changes) |
| Survey redesigns (e.g. Canadian Community Health Survey) | Statistics Canada health series | Break in trend; pre- and post-redesign estimates differ |
| Indicator-definition updates | CIHI indicators | Rebased or redefined indicators reset their own series |

## URL verification

As part of M2, every catalogued URL was checked for reachability with
`python3 -m sohbc check --all`. All catalogued landing pages and the one
automated download endpoint returned HTTP 200 at the time of checking
(24 sources). The federal publisher's own portal was unreachable from the
verification environment, so federal open data is reached through the
Open Government portal record instead; this is noted on that catalogue
entry.

## Governance

- **Licences vary** by source (open-government licences to publisher
  terms). Each catalogue entry records its licence; redistribution of
  anything committed must respect it.
- **No individual-level data** in the repository — a hard rule.
- **First Nations data** are governed by the First Nations principles of
  OCAP® and specific agreements; they are cited for context, not
  redistributed [@fnigcOcap].
- **"Best use" standard.** A source backed only by published summary
  statistics is admissible when it passes licence and governance checks —
  the goal is the best use of all publicly available information that can
  be appropriately used.

## Keeping this current

Add an entry here whenever ingesting a source surfaces a problem, and
update the [catalogue](data-sources.qmd) when a gap closes. See
[How to ingest a source](../how-to/ingest-data.qmd).
